boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Rose Hill destinations for studying, gathering, campus rituals, and noticing Fordham’s shared history.

cards.title: Walsh Family Library
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill campus library
cards.notes: Set up for a study session in the library, then check its live hours page before planning an evening visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with regular-session late closing on most weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham lists Walsh Library at Rose Hill with regular-session hours until midnight Monday through Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Regular-session hours shown by Fordham: Mon–Thu and Sun until 12 a.m.; hours may change by semester.

cards.title: LITE Center
cards.subtitle: Walsh Library lower level, Room 014
cards.notes: Use the collaboration areas for a group work block, or plan a project around its makerspace and recording rooms.
cards.short_summary: A technology workspace with collaboration, XR, recording, and making facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says Rose Hill students have free access to the LITE Center’s collaboration areas, recording rooms, XR space, and makerspace.
cards.access_notes: Fordham locates it in Walsh Library lower level, Room 014; the page lists Monday–Thursday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: McShane Campus Center First Floor
cards.subtitle: McShane Campus Center, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Meet at a communal table for a low-key work session, or take a break in the lounge and pool area.
cards.short_summary: A student-facing floor built around lounging, pool, and communal tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham describes the first floor as a gathering space where students play pool, relax in the lounge, and work at communal tables.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Joseph M. McShane, S.J., Campus Center; check building access before visiting.

cards.title: Campus Center Lawn
cards.subtitle: At McShane Campus Center, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Use the named lawn as a simple outdoor meeting point, then move indoors if weather or campus programming changes.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor destination directly identified on Fordham’s Rose Hill map.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Rose Hill campus map lists Campus Center Lawn as part of the McShane Campus Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; availability can be affected by weather and scheduled events.

cards.title: Edwards Parade
cards.subtitle: Historic quadrangle at Rose Hill
cards.notes: Walk through the quad and read its context before an event; it is also the destination for Fordham’s commencement procession.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus quadrangle tied to University Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies Edwards Parade as a traditional college quadrangle and says the commencement procession moves to its entrance.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area; respect any event setup, posted boundaries, and University directions.

cards.title: Keating Steps
cards.subtitle: Outside Keating Hall, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Pause at the steps during a campus walk and use the occasion to look toward Edwards Parade and the terrace below.
cards.short_summary: A named Rose Hill landmark used for an official Senior Week class-photo event.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s 2026 Senior Week schedule places the Always a Ram Celebration and Class of 2026 Photo at Keating Steps.
cards.source_title: Senior Week at Rose Hill | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Exterior steps; keep clear during ceremonies, scheduled photography, and active building access.

cards.title: Terrace of the Presidents
cards.subtitle: Between Edwards Parade and Keating Hall
cards.notes: Walk the granite steps slowly and look for the engraved names of honorary-degree recipients rather than treating it as a shortcut.
cards.short_summary: A stair terrace whose engraved stones record visiting heads of state.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says the granite steps between Edwards Parade and the Keating Hall Terrace carry names of heads of state who received honorary doctorates.
cards.access_notes: Exterior steps on the Rose Hill campus; use normal pedestrian care and honor event access controls.

cards.title: Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: In front of the Rose Hill Gymnasium
cards.notes: Find the bell outside the gym and read the nearby context; save ringing or event participation for authorized University occasions.
cards.short_summary: A historic ship’s bell that marks commencement and Fordham athletic victories.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham states that the Victory Bell stands in front of the Rose Hill gymnasium, begins commencement, and traditionally peals after Ram victories.
cards.access_notes: View from the gym exterior; do not assume public permission to ring or handle the bell.

cards.title: Carolyn Dursi Cunniffe Fountain
cards.subtitle: Near Cunniffe House, Rose Hill
cards.notes: Add the fountain to a walk between Keating and nearby halls, and keep the stop brief if the surrounding paths are busy.
cards.short_summary: A named Rose Hill fountain associated with Cunniffe House.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies the Carolyn Dursi Cunniffe Fountain as one of two Rose Hill campus landmarks named for Maurice and Carolyn Cunniffe.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; observe posted restrictions and do not enter the fountain area.

cards.title: 9/11 Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill campus memorial garden
cards.notes: Visit quietly as part of a campus walk, allowing space for reflection and for anyone using the memorial area.
cards.short_summary: A named memorial garden marked on Fordham’s Rose Hill campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Rose Hill campus map identifies the 9/11 Memorial Garden as a named campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Memorial setting on campus; keep the visit respectful and follow any posted guidance.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Fordham rituals, annual gatherings, and campus-specific customs centered on Rose Hill and the Fordham community.

cards.entity_name: Victory Bell Ringing After Ram Victories
cards.title: Ring the Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill Gymnasium, Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: After a Fordham athletic win, look for the gathering at the bell by Rose Hill Gym; the university identifies its ringing as a continuing Ram-victory custom.
cards.short_summary: A World War II ship’s bell becomes Fordham’s post-victory sound.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham states that the Victory Bell traditionally peals following Ram victories.
cards.access_notes: Observe from public campus areas during an athletic victory; event access can vary.

cards.title: Begin Commencement With the Bell
cards.subtitle: Edwards Parade, Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: At commencement, listen for the Victory Bell that starts the academic procession; Fordham’s current ceremony information places the sound at the procession’s opening.
cards.short_summary: The bell is not just for sports—it also signals Fordham’s graduation procession.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says the academic procession begins at the sound of the Victory Bell and identifies bell-ringing as the beginning of University Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Commencement participation and guest entry follow the university’s current ceremony instructions.

cards.title: Ride the Bronze Ram
cards.subtitle: Between Dealy Hall and Hughes Hall, Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: Find the bronze ram between Dealy and Hughes during a campus walk; student media documents the first-year superstition of riding it within the first 10 days.
cards.short_summary: A bronze campus ram anchors a playful first-year superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fordham Ram reports that first-year students traditionally ride the bronze ram within their first 10 days to avoid bad luck.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Fordham | The Fordham Ram
cards.access_notes: A casual photo stop on campus; do not climb or use the statue in a way that could damage it.

cards.title: Breakfast During Finals Week
cards.subtitle: Fordham campuses, before finals
cards.notes: Watch campus announcements near finals for Midnight Breakfast, a Fordham finals-week tradition; commuter services specifically identifies it as an event offered before finals.
cards.short_summary: Fordham marks finals season with breakfast at midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says it offers Midnight Breakfast for students right before finals, and Fordham Now describes it as a long-running finals-week tradition.
cards.source_title: Events and Activities for Rose Hill Commuters | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Check current student communications for date, campus, eligibility, and any required RSVP.

cards.title: Take the Commuter-Friendly Finals Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill commuter programming
cards.notes: Commuters can look for Midday Breakfast on a late-class-day near finals; Fordham says it was created so students unable to stay for Midnight Breakfast can join in.
cards.short_summary: A daytime companion to Fordham’s Midnight Breakfast for commuters.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham describes Midday Breakfast as a commuter-friendly event held near finals when students cannot stay for Midnight Breakfast.
cards.source_title: Events and Activities for Rose Hill Commuters | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Check Commuter Student Services for the semester’s date, location, and attendance details.

cards.title: Join Spring Weekend
cards.subtitle: Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: Follow Campus Activities Board and Residence Hall Association announcements for the spring program; student media documents its music, comedy, guest, and dance components.
cards.short_summary: Fordham’s spring-semester campus celebration combines programmed entertainment and a dance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fordham Ram identifies Spring Weekend as a Fordham tradition organized with music, comedy, a guest appearance, and a Residence Hall Association dance.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Fordham | The Fordham Ram
cards.access_notes: Programming, venues, and entry rules vary by year; use current Campus Activities Board information.

cards.title: Hear the Finals-Week Howl
cards.subtitle: Keating Hall Steps, Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: If finals-week student posts announce the gathering, head to the Keating steps to listen or join the collective howl; it is described as student-organized rather than official.
cards.short_summary: Students gather at Keating during finals for one loud release of stress.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fordham Ram reports that students gather on Keating Steps on one finals-week night for a collective howl and that the activity is student-organized.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Fordham | The Fordham Ram
cards.access_notes: This is informally organized; follow current student notices and respect quiet-hour and safety rules.

cards.title: Start a Veteran’s Fordham Journey at the Bell
cards.subtitle: Victory Bell, Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: Eligible incoming student veterans can check with Military and Veterans’ Services about orientation; Fordham documents the bell ringing as an annual marker of the academic start.
cards.short_summary: Fordham’s veteran community uses the Victory Bell as a ceremonial beginning.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham reports that new student veterans cap orientation by ringing the Victory Bell, an annual tradition signifying the start of their academic careers.
cards.source_title: Fordham Veterans Association Welcomes New Students
cards.access_notes: This ceremonial activity is intended for the student-veteran orientation program; confirm eligibility with the office.

cards.title: Hear Lessons and Carols
cards.subtitle: University Church, Rose Hill campus
cards.notes: Plan for the annual December performance at the University Church when announced; Fordham’s program combines university choirs with music, dance, and reflection.
cards.short_summary: Fordham’s seasonal choral tradition brings performers to the University Church.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham calls the Festival of Lessons and Carols an annual tradition and lists a Rose Hill performance at the University Church with no tickets or registration required.
cards.source_title: Festival of Lessons and Carols | Fordham
cards.access_notes: The cited program says no tickets or registration are required; confirm the current year’s date and venue before going.

cards.title: Choose an Honors Last Lecture
cards.subtitle: Fordham College at Rose Hill Honors Program
cards.notes: Honors seniors select an influential faculty member, who then gives a spring “last lecture”; look to the Honors events calendar for that year’s date and location.
cards.short_summary: Fordham Honors seniors turn a faculty favorite into a spring lecture tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham states that Honors seniors choose an influential faculty member to give the Honors Last Lecture, usually held in late March or early April.
cards.access_notes: This is an FCRH Honors Program event; check the Honors calendar for current attendance details.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Fordham University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe Rose Hill sequence that starts with orientation and campus bearings, then leaves room for study, reflection, clubs, and an evening coffeehouse stop.

cards.title: Start with orientation
cards.subtitle: First stop: Rose Hill orientation
cards.notes: Use the official orientation schedule to find your group, ask where key offices are, and introduce yourself to someone in your session.
cards.short_summary: Fordham frames Rose Hill orientation as a resource-and-connection starting point for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says Rose Hill orientation helps new students learn about resources and meet people, with fall orientation scheduled for August 22–25, 2026.
cards.source_title: Student Orientation at Rose Hill | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Follow the current Orientation Guidebook schedule and instructions from Fordham.

cards.title: Get your bearings on foot
cards.subtitle: Next: a self-paced campus loop
cards.notes: Take the self-guided route at an easy pace and mark the buildings you will actually use during your first week.
cards.short_summary: A guided route offers a practical first pass through Rose Hill’s core spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham offers a year-round Rose Hill self-guided tour, generally available on weekdays and most weekends, with preset walking trails.
cards.access_notes: Registration windows and availability vary; use Fordham’s visit page before setting out.

cards.title: Pause on Eddie's Parade
cards.subtitle: A central outdoor reset
cards.notes: Meet your new group outside for a few minutes, then use the open space as a landmark before heading to the next building.
cards.short_summary: Orientation materials depict new students gathering on Eddie’s Parade.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Rose Hill orientation page identifies Eddie’s Parade as the setting for groups of students during New Student Orientation.
cards.source_title: Student Orientation at Rose Hill | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access and programming depend on current campus conditions and schedules.

cards.title: Find Keating Hall
cards.subtitle: A recognizable Rose Hill landmark
cards.notes: Walk up to Keating, note its entrances, and snap a reference photo so you can navigate confidently when classes begin.
cards.short_summary: Keating anchors the campus scene shown in Fordham’s Rose Hill visit materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s visit page features students relaxing and walking on the grass in front of Keating Hall at Rose Hill.
cards.access_notes: Use the current Rose Hill campus map and observe building-entry rules.

cards.title: Set up a library fallback
cards.subtitle: Study stop: Walsh Library at Rose Hill
cards.notes: Locate a floor you would be comfortable using between classes, then save the library hours page for changes during the term.
cards.short_summary: Walsh Library provides a dependable academic stop with regular-session evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham lists Walsh Library at Rose Hill and posts regular-session hours through midnight Monday through Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Regular-session hours shown are Mon–Thu 8:30 a.m.–12 a.m. and Sun 10 a.m.–12 a.m.; Fordham notes hours may change.

cards.title: Step into University Church
cards.subtitle: A quiet Rose Hill landmark
cards.notes: If a service is underway, follow posted guidance; otherwise, use the church area as a calm point to regroup and orient yourself.
cards.short_summary: The University Church is a listed Rose Hill sacred space and a site for campus liturgies.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham lists University Church among Rose Hill sacred spaces and posts summer Sunday Mass there at 10 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Check Fordham Campus Ministry’s current schedule; the cited page lists summer Sunday Mass at 10 a.m.

cards.title: Try a low-pressure club meeting
cards.subtitle: Activity option: Chess Club
cards.notes: Use Rams Involved to confirm the next meeting, then arrive ready to play one casual game and ask how beginners can participate.
cards.short_summary: Chess Club offers a straightforward way to meet peers around a shared activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Rose Hill organization directory says Chess Club provides weekly peer play and hosts internal and intercollegiate tournaments.
cards.access_notes: Meeting details require student access to Rams Involved or confirmation from the organization.

cards.title: Check the weekend program
cards.subtitle: Activity option: Campus Activities Board
cards.notes: Look for the next CAB weekend listing and choose a campus or city activity whose time, meeting point, and requirements are clearly posted.
cards.short_summary: CAB’s Weekend Activities Committee plans recurring weekend programming and excursions.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says the Campus Activities Board’s Weekend Activities Committee provides weekend programming on and off campus, ranging from bingo to excursions.
cards.source_title: Rose Hill Campus Activities Board | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Dates, destinations, registration, and any costs vary by program; verify the current CAB announcement.

cards.entity_name: Joseph M. McShane, S.J. Campus Center
cards.title: Locate McShane Campus Center
cards.subtitle: A useful student-life waypoint
cards.notes: Find the main entrances and save the building on your map; it is a practical place to recognize before your first full week.
cards.short_summary: McShane Campus Center is a named Rose Hill destination on Fordham’s official map.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s official Rose Hill Campus Map lists McShane Campus Center as a campus building.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current building access and event locations through Fordham before visiting.

cards.title: End at Rodrigue's
cards.subtitle: Evening option: Alumni House
cards.notes: Confirm that night’s programming, then stop in for an open mic, creative event, or a quiet drink-free coffeehouse visit with classmates.
cards.short_summary: Rodrigue’s combines coffeehouse service with student-planned creative programming in Alumni House.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies Rodrigue’s as its student-run coffee house in Alumni House and lists open mics, arts events, and regular evening hours.
cards.source_title: Rose Hill Campus Activities Board | Fordham
cards.access_notes: Fordham lists Mon–Thu and Sun hours until 12 a.m.; confirm current hours and event access before going.
